brief.problem: Relay is a frontline operations platform ("system of action for physical operations") that captures spoken operational knowledge from frontline workers and turns it into structured signals, dashboards and automated decision support [4] [9]. It ships an "Operational Insights" product with continuous monitoring and performance trend dashboards to its own customers [2] [6], and processes over 1 billion data points weekly across 35+ languages [8]. Internally, its Customer Success org appears to use Metabase alongside HubSpot and Claude for activity/behavior analysis [1]. With a fresh $36M raise (Sept 2026) aimed at scaling frontline safety and operational intelligence [3], the pressure is on both to harden its customer-facing analytics (Operational Insights, Dashboard) and to scale internal reporting as the company grows headcount fast (Inc. 5000, Deloitte Fast 500 recognition) [9] [5].

expansion.core_insight: Relay processes over 1 billion weekly data points into customer-facing 'Operational Insights' and internal CS Metabase reports, creating a massive governance and scaling challenge following their $36M raise [1] [3] [8].

seats.top_concern: Metric mismatch between internal Metabase/HubSpot view and customer-facing Operational Insights dashboard as scale grows [1] [2] [8].
No proof Metabase is failing or that current custom build is slowing revenue; switching cost unjustified this fiscal year.
Metabase already integrated with HubSpot and fits CS workflow; a semantic-layer project adds complexity, not speed [1].
Wants internal CS metrics and customer-facing dashboard metrics to agree without manual SQL reconciliation.
No confirmed warehouse underlying the 1B+ weekly data points, so scope of migration and effort is unknown [8].

turns.says: We have a real metric mismatch: Metabase shows one version of behavior change, the customer-facing Operational Insights dashboard shows another [1] [2]. As we scale past the $36M raise [3], that gap gets expensive to maintain by hand.

I hear the pain, but I need evidence Metabase itself is breaking, not just that two systems disagree. We already pay for Metabase; switching cost has to be justified by something more than inconvenience.
Metabase is already wired into HubSpot and the CS workflow [1]. A semantic-layer migration right after a funding raise is a distraction from scaling frontline safety, not a speed-up.
I spend real time manually reconciling what I see in Metabase against what customers see in their Dashboard. If Omni can close that gap, my day-to-day gets easier.
Before I can size this, I need to know what's underneath the 1 billion weekly data points [8]. No warehouse is confirmed, so I can't tell you if this is a BI swap or a platform re-architecture.

outcome.label: Coin flip
outcome.summary: A narrow, CS-scoped pilot on metric consistency is plausible; the Head of Data and customer want it, but the CFO and unresolved warehouse/architecture unknowns keep it from being more than a coin flip.
